source.author: lucan
source.text: Libycae quod fertile terrae est, Vergit in occasus: sed et haec non fontibus ullis Solvitur: Arctoos raris Aquilonibus imbres Accipit, et nostris reficit sua rura serenis.
source.text_original: Libycae quod fertile terrae est, / Vergit in occasus: sed et haec non fontibus ullis / Solvitur: Arctoos raris Aquilonibus imbres / Accipit, et nostris reficit sua rura serenis.
source.text_english: What is fertile in the Libyan land slopes toward the west; but even this is not watered by any springs: it receives rains from the north winds of the North, and with our clear skies it refreshes its own fields.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quotiens raucos ad litoris ictus deficiam Scythicum metuens pontumque polumque nec de te credam nostris ingrata serenis.
reuse.text_original: quotiens raucos ad litoris ictus / deficiam Scythicum metuens pontumque polumque / nec de te credam nostris ingrata serenis.
reuse.text_english: How often shall I faint at the hoarse beatings of the shore, fearing the Scythian sea and the sky alike, and in our fair weather shall I not believe a thing about you, ungrateful one?
